about: Known differences between server/schema.sql and its copies (F-33). May only shrink: the check fails on a difference not listed here, on an entry that no longer matches a difference, and (with --ratchet) on an entry the base commit's copy of this file does not have. Every group needs a reason. README.md explains the keys.

groups.reason: server/src/db.js ensureSchema() creates only the tables added after the original schema. The base tables come from server/schema.sql alone (MySQL initdb in deploy/docker-compose.yml), imported_events also from the importer's ensureImportSchema(). A database not built from schema.sql never gets them. Open part of F-33, not fixed in PR 1.

seed.js's ban_evidence retrofit predates the source column. The column is not lost: db.js ensureSchema(), which runs on every server start, adds ban_evidence.source at the reference's position (the db.js alter pass compares it without a difference).

Stock Laravel skeleton tables for sessions and queues. The deploy runs Laravel with SESSION_DRIVER=array and QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync (deploy/docker-compose.yml) and never runs Laravel migrations (api/docker/entrypoint.sh); only a local `composer setup` creates these tables. (The cache tables are in server/schema.sql since the deploy uses CACHE_STORE=database.)
Laravel's own migration ledger, created by `php artisan migrate` itself; it is not part of the application schema.

The stock Laravel skeleton users migration lacks the application's profile, moderation, terms and two-factor columns and their unique indexes. server/schema.sql owns the users table and the deploy never runs Laravel migrations (api/docker/entrypoint.sh), so the skeleton only shapes a local `composer setup` database. A new users column still needs a Laravel migration (see README.md).

server/schema.sql keeps users.password nullable for accounts created through Google sign-in, which have no password; the stock skeleton declares it NOT NULL. Same scope as the group above: the skeleton only shapes a local `composer setup` database.
entries: laravel/migrate column-attr users.password nullable ref="YES" copy="NO"
